steps: Boil a kettle and fill the saucepan; bring to the boil on the hob for the noodles.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, then cut the red peppers into short thin strips.
Peel the carrots and cut them into thin matchsticks or small pieces, so they soften quickly and are safe for a toddler.
Cook the noodles for 4 minutes or to the packet time, drain and snip into short lengths.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then stir-fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white and cooked through.
Add the carrots and peppers and fry for 4–5 minutes until soft, then toss in the noodles with half the soy sauce, taste, and add more only if needed.
pitfalls: Too much soy sauce makes the dish salty for a toddler, so add it gradually and use less than you think.
Thick chicken strips or carrot pieces stay undercooked or hard to chew, so cut everything small and thin.
Overcooked noodles go soft and clump in the wok, so drain them promptly and toss with a little oil.
output.tip: Cut a portion of the noodles shorter with kitchen scissors once cooked, so they are easy for a toddler to manage.

steps: Boil a kettle and bring a large saucepan of unsalted water to the boil for the noodles.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin, short strips and cut the red pepper into small pieces.
Cut the carrots into thin matchsticks or small pieces, about 3cm long, so they soften quickly and are safe for a toddler.
Cook the noodles in the unsalted water for 4–5 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots and pepper and stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until soft, then toss in the noodles with the soy sauce diluted with a splash of water. Cool before serving.
pitfalls: Using the full amount of undiluted soy sauce makes the dish far too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water and add it gradually.
Leaving carrots in chunky pieces keeps them hard and tough for a toddler to chew, so cut them very thin and cook until soft.
Overcrowding the wok steams the chicken and leaves it pale and rubbery, so cook it in two batches if needed.
output.tip: Cut the noodles into shorter lengths with kitchen scissors after draining so they are easier for a toddler to eat.

equipment: Large wok or deep frying pan
steps: Boil a kettle and put the noodles in a large saucepan of unsalted water to cook for 4–5 minutes, then drain.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin, short strips about 1cm wide for small mouths.
Cut the red peppers into thin short strips and grate or thinly slice the carrots so they soften quickly.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat, then fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots for 2 minutes, then the red peppers for 2–3 minutes, until soft enough to squash between your fingers.
Toss in the noodles with the soy sauce and 2 tbsp of water, then cut the noodles shorter with scissors and cool before serving.
pitfalls: Adding the soy sauce at full strength makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with a little water.
Leaving the chicken in large pieces or undercooking it is a choking and food safety risk, so slice it small and check there is no pink.
Overcooking the noodles makes them clump and go gummy, so drain them while they still have a little bite.
output.tip: Cut the noodles into short lengths with kitchen scissors so they are easier for a toddler to eat.

steps: Boil a kettle and chop the onion finely; mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion for 5–6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then turn the heat up and brown the beef mince in two batches, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well, then simmer gently, partly covered, for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
About 12 minutes before serving, boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente, following the packet time.
Reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, then toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening with pasta water if needed.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan steams the mince grey instead of browning it, so cook it in two batches over high heat.
Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter, so add it only for 30 seconds before the meat.
Rinsing the spaghetti washes off starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Finish the spaghetti in the sauce for 1 minute with a splash of pasta water so it absorbs the flavour.

steps: Fill a large saucepan with salted water and bring it to the boil on a high heat.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the beef mince, breaking it up and browning it for 8–10 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti for 10–11 minutes, until al dente, reserving a mug of pasta water before draining. Toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so brown it in two batches if needed.
Under-seasoning the sauce leaves it flat and acidic from the tomatoes, so taste and adjust before serving.
Draining the spaghetti and leaving it to sit makes it clump and go sticky, so toss it with the sauce straight away.
output.tip: Add a splash of the starchy pasta water to the sauce when tossing; it helps the sauce cling to every strand.

steps: Start the sauce first: finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the beef mince over high heat. Break it up and brown for 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well, then simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the sauce simmers, boil salted water in the saucepan, then cook the spaghetti for 9–11 minutes until al dente.
Reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, then toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening with a splash of the water.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so let the pan get hot and brown the mince in two batches if needed.
Cooking the garlic too long over high heat makes it bitter, so add it only for 30 seconds before the mince.
Rinsing the spaghetti after draining washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Stir a spoonful of the starchy pasta water into the sauce at the end to make it glossy and help it coat the spaghetti.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion and pepper for 8–10 minutes until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thickened and no longer watery.
Make four wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5–7 minutes on low heat until the whites are set.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and toast it; serve straight from the pan.
pitfalls: Adding eggs to thin, watery sauce makes them sink and the whites spread, so reduce the sauce until it coats a spoon.
Cooking the eggs on a high heat with the lid on leaves hard yolks and a scorched base, so keep the heat low and check from 5 minutes.
Under-cooking the pepper and onion leaves a raw, sharp flavour, so soften them fully before adding the tomatoes.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it in gently and avoid broken yolks or stray shell.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces before heating the pan.
Fry the onion and red pepper in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thick and jammy; meanwhile, slice the bread.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook over low heat for 5–7 minutes.
Remove from the heat when the whites are set but the yolks still wobble, then serve with the bread.
pitfalls: Watery sauce makes the eggs slide around and cook unevenly, so reduce it until it holds a spoon trail.
Cooking the eggs over high heat sets the yolks hard and leaves the whites rubbery, so keep the heat low with the lid on.
Undercooked peppers stay crunchy and taste raw, so soften them fully before adding the tomatoes.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it into the sauce without breaking the yolk.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces.
Fry the onion and pepper in olive oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thick and jammy.
Make four wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes.
While the eggs cook, warm the bread in an oven at 180°C, then slice it for serving.
pitfalls: A thin, watery sauce lets the eggs slide around and cook unevenly, so reduce it until a spoon leaves a trail.
Cooking the eggs over high heat turns the whites rubbery and the yolks hard, so keep it low and covered.
Adding the eggs before the pepper is soft leaves the dish raw-tasting and crunchy, so cook the base fully first.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it gently into its well without breaking the yolk.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead, then heat the oven to 220°C. Rub the beef with oil, salt, pepper, rosemary, thyme and crushed garlic.
Whisk the flour, eggs and milk with a pinch of salt into a smooth batter. Rest it for at least 30 minutes.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C. Cook 50–60 minutes more for medium, to 55–60°C in the centre.
While the beef roasts, parboil the peeled potatoes for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake roughly. Roast them in hot oil on a tray for 60–70 minutes, turning once.
Add the parsnips and carrots in butter to the oven 40 minutes before the end. Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes while the oven rises to 230°C.

Heat the oil in the pudding tin until smoking, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes. Boil the broccoli for 3–4 minutes; make gravy from the tin juices, wine and stock, and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven during the first 15 minutes of baking makes the Yorkshire puddings collapse, so keep the door shut.
Pouring batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so wait until the oil is smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves it dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Rough up the parboiled potatoes in the colander so the scuffed edges turn extra crisp in the hot fat.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C, then roast the beef with garlic, rosemary and thyme for 20 minutes. Reduce to 180°C and cook for about 1 hour 10 minutes for medium.
While the oven heats, peel and cut the potatoes and parsnips, then parboil the potatoes for 8–10 minutes. Drain, shake roughly and leave to steam dry.
Mix the Yorkshire batter and rest it for at least 30 minutes. Toss the potatoes and parsnips in hot oil and roast at 200°C for 60–70 minutes, turning once.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 230°C and heat the oil in the Yorkshire tin for 10 minutes until smoking hot.
Pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the door. Meanwhile, make the gravy in the beef tin with red wine, stock and juices, simmering until slightly thickened.
Boil the carrots for 8–10 minutes, then steam the broccoli for 3–4 minutes. Toss both in butter, carve the beef thinly and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings bake lets the heat escape, so they sink and turn flat.
Putting batter into lukewarm fat stops the puddings rising, so wait until the oil is smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour before roasting so it cooks evenly and the centre does not stay cold.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Take the beef out of the fridge, rub with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and seasoning.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter. Rest it for at least 30 minutes.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C for about 60 minutes for medium. Check for 55–60°C in the centre.
While the beef cooks, parboil the potatoes for 8–10 minutes and drain. Shake to roughen the edges, then roast in hot oil for 60 minutes.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the Yorkshire tin for 10 minutes, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes.
Roast the carrots and parsnips alongside the potatoes for 40 minutes. Make gravy in the beef tin with wine and stock, simmer 8–10 minutes, then steam the broccoli for 4 minutes.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings cook makes them collapse, so keep it shut for the first 20 minutes.
Putting batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so wait until the oil is smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves it dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Use the resting time for the oven-hungry Yorkshire puddings and gravy, and slice the beef thinly against the grain just before serving.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken straight from the marinade into the pan lets the thick yoghurt coating catch and split, so wipe off the excess and brown in two batches to avoid steaming.
Cooking the rice at the end leaves the curry sitting and thickening, so start the rice about 15 minutes before the curry finishes so both are ready together.
Skipping a taste before serving leaves the sauce flat or sharp from the tinned tomatoes, so season with salt and a pinch of sugar at the end.
output.tip: Stir a spoonful of yoghurt or a splash of double cream into the curry off the heat, then finish with chopped fresh coriander for a smoother, rounder sauce.

pitfalls: Putting all the marinated chicken into the pan at once drops the temperature, so it stews grey instead of browning; brown it in two batches.
Simmering without a lid or any added liquid can leave the sauce thick and catching on the base, so stir occasionally and add a splash of water if it reduces too far.
Adding the yoghurt marinade straight into hot tomatoes at a hard boil can split the sauce; keep it at a gentle simmer after the chicken goes back in.
output.tip: Cook the rice while the curry simmers and rest it covered for 5 minutes off the heat, then finish the curry with a squeeze of lemon juice and chopped coriander to lift the flavour.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken with its thick coating of yoghurt marinade to a very hot pan can make the yoghurt split and turn grainy, so lift the pieces out, shake off the excess and brown over medium-high heat.
Cooking the tomatoes for only the stated time without tasting leaves the sauce sharp and thin, so season with salt at the end and add a pinch of sugar if it tastes acidic.
Cooking the rice at the last minute or without rinsing it gives a sticky, clumped result, so rinse the 300g until the water runs clear and start it as the curry begins to simmer.
output.tip: Finish the curry with a spoonful of yoghurt or a splash of double cream and a pinch of garam masala off the heat for a rounder, more fragrant sauce.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or cooking them before the vegetables, leaves them soft and clumping in the wok; soak or boil until just pliable, then rinse and drain well.
Adding the soy sauce while the pan is still very hot, or adding too much, makes it burn and turn the stir-fry too salty; add it off the fiercest heat and taste before adding more.
Cutting the broccoli into large, uneven florets means the stalks stay raw while the tops overcook; cut them into small, even pieces of about 2cm.
output.tip: Shake off excess cornstarch and fry the tofu in a single layer without moving it for 2–3 minutes per side, so a firm golden crust forms before you turn it.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or adding them to the wok still wet, turns them gummy and clumpy, so soak until just pliable, drain well and toss with a little oil.
Adding soy sauce all at once to a crowded, cooler wok makes the vegetables stew rather than sear, so add it in a thin stream over high heat for the last 30–60 seconds.
Cutting the broccoli into uneven or large florets leaves some pieces raw while others overcook, so keep them to about 2–3cm.
output.tip: Pat the pressed tofu dry with kitchen paper and fry it in a single layer in about 2cm of hot oil at roughly 180°C, leaving each side undisturbed for 2–3 minutes so the coating sets and doesn't stick.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or adding them to the wok undrained, makes them gummy and clumpy, so soak until just pliable and drain well.
Adding the soy sauce while the tofu is still in the pan, or leaving the crisp tofu in the sauce for more than a minute, turns the coating soggy.
Crowding the frying pan with all the tofu at once drops the temperature and makes the cornstarch coating patchy and sticky, so fry in two batches.
output.tip: Cut the broccoli into small, even florets and add a splash of water, about 30ml, to the wok, covering for 1 minute, so the stalks cook through while the pepper stays crunchy.

steps: Pane riisi keema: loputa riis, lisa potti külma vett ja veidi vähem soola kui tavaliselt, keeda kaane all 12–15 minutit.
Haki sibulad peeneks ja riivi porgandid jämedalt, lõika kanafilee 2 cm tükkideks.
Kuumuta pannil õli ja hauta sibulat ning porgandit 5 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa kana ja prae 6–7 minutit, kuni liha on igast küljest valkjas ja veidi kuldne.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit, kuni kana on läbi küpsenud.
Sega hapukoor kastmesse, soojenda 1–2 minutit ilma keetmata ja maitse üle. Soola lisa ainult vajadusel, puljongikuubik on juba soolane.
pitfalls: Ära soola kastet enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik annab juba soola ja väike laps saab liiga soolase toidu.
Ära keeda kastet pärast hapukoore lisamist: hapukoor läheb lõhki ja kaste muutub tombuliseks.
Ära lõika kanatükke liiga suureks ega küpseta liiga kaua: liha jääb kuiv ja kõva.
output.tip: Maitsesta täiskasvanute taldrikul soola ja pipart alles laual, siis jääb laste portsjon vähese soolaga.

equipment: Suur sügav pann või kastrul kaanega
steps: Pane riis sooja vee all loputatult kaanega potti, lisa vesi ja keeda 12–15 minutit vaikselt, soola lisa riisi vette vaid näpuotsaga või jäta üldse ära.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgandid jämedalt, samal ajal kui riisivesi kuumeneb.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm suurusteks kuubikuteks ja prae kuumal õlitatud pannil 5–6 minutit kuldseks.
Lisa pannile sibul ja porgand ning hauta 5 minutit pehmeks.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit. Soola lisa ainult siis, kui maitsed ja vaja on, sest kuubik on juba soolane.
Sega hapukoor lõpus sisse, soojenda 1–2 minutit ilma keetmata ja serveeri riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära lisa lisasoola enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik on juba soolane ja road muutuvad väikesele lapsele liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda hapukoort kõrgel kuumusel: see hakkab kokku kerkima ja kaste muutub tombuliseks.
Ära prae kanatükke liiga tihedalt pannil: liha hakkab hauduma, mitte pruunistuma, ja jääb kuivaks.
output.tip: Maitsesta kaste lõpus ja lisa vajadusel sidrunimahla või musta pipart, siis ei vaja roog soola ning sobib ka lapsele.

equipment: Suur sügav pann või kastrul kaanega
steps: Pane riis pesemata kuumale veele või loputa see sõelal ja pane kaanega potti keema, vett vastavalt pakendi juhisele. Keeda vaiksel tulel 12–15 minutit.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgand jämedalt, samal ajal kui riis keeb.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm kuubikuteks.
Kuumuta pannil õli ja hauta sibulat ning porgandit 4–5 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa kana ja prae 6–8 minutit, kuni liha on igast küljest valge.

Sega puljongikuubik 200 ml kuuma veega, kalla pannile ja hauta kaane all 8 minutit. Lisa hapukoor, sega ja soojenda 2 minutit, ära lase keema. Soola lisa vaid siis, kui maitsmisel tundub vaja, sest puljongikuubik on juba soolane.
pitfalls: Ära soola kana ega kastet enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik annab juba soola ja väikesele lapsele läheb roog liiga soolaseks.
Ära lase hapukoorel pärast lisamist keema minna: kaste lõheneb ja muutub kärnaliseks.
Ära kata kana liiga kõrgel kuumusel kaane alla: liha kuivab ära ja muutub kummiseks.
output.tip: Kasuta puljongikuubikut pool kogusest ja lisa maitseks rohkem sibulat või porgandit, siis jääb roog väiksema soolaga ka lapsele sobivaks.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja pane hapukapsas pottu eelkuumutatud kohta, et see saaks kohe hauduma hakata.
Haki sibul ja lõika sealiha 3 cm suurusteks tükkideks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumal rasval kõigilt külgedelt pruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, nõrutatud odrakruubid, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et kate on peaaegu kaetud, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1,5–2 tundi.
Prae või keeda kuni valmimiseni, sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel vett, et põhi ei kõiguks.
Koori ja tükelda kartulid, lisa need potti viimase 30–40 minuti jooksul ning hauta pehmeks, seejärel muserda osa kartulitest, et roog pakseneks.
pitfalls: Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma vedelikuta: kruubid ja kapsas kõrbevad põhja.
Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja roog kaotab tekstuuri.
Ära jäta hapukapsast väga hapuks loputamata, kui see on terav: roog jääb liiga hapuks ja kruubid ei pehmene korralikult.
output.tip: Mulgikapsad on järgmisel päeval veel paremad, sest maitsed ühinevad, nii et küpseta need võimalusel eelmisel õhtul valmis.

equipment: Väike pott odrakruubi leotamiseks või eelkeetmiseks
steps: Loputa odrakruup ja leota seda külmas vees, kuni valmistad ülejäänu ette (või keeda 20 minutit eelnevalt pehmeks).
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Kuumuta pott, prae sealiha osade kaupa pruuniks ja lisa sibul, prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas koos vedelikuga, loorberilehed, nõrutatud kruubid ja nii palju vett, et see katab kõik peaaegu. Lase kaane all vaikselt podiseda 1 tund.
Kooru ja tükelda kartulid 3 cm tükkideks ning lisa potti, kui ülejäänud on veerand tunni jagu pehmenenud; hauta veel 40–50 minutit, kuni kruubid ja liha on pehmed.
Sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel kuuma vett, et põhi ei kõrbeks; maitsesta soolaga ja lase enne serveerimist 10 minutit seista.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja kaotavad kuju.
Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ega lase vedelikul ära kuivada: kruubid imavad vett ja põhi kõrbeb kergesti põhja.
Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: kapsas ja selle vedelik on juba soolased ja roog võib üle soolatud saada.
output.tip: Kui hapukapsas on väga hapu, loputa see enne külma veega kergelt läbi, siis jääb maitse pehmemaks.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees, kuni muud asjad valmis saavad, ja nõruta enne kasutamist.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm tükkideks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumas rasvas igast küljest pruuniks, siis lisa sibul ja prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja odrakruubid, kata veega ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1,5 tundi.
Koori ja tükelda kartulid ning lisa potti, kui kapsas on tund aega haudunud. Hauta veel 30–40 minutit, kuni kruup ja kartul on pehmed.
Maitsesta soola ja pipraga, sega läbi ning lase 10 minutit seista, enne kui serveerid.
pitfalls: Ära jäta potti ilma järelevalveta ja vett lisamata: kruup imab vedeliku endasse ning põhi kõrbeb põhja.
Ära lisa kartuleid kohe algusest: need keevad pudruks ja mulgikapsas kaotab oma tekstuuri.
Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: kapsas on juba soolane ja roog läheb liiga soolaseks.
output.tip: Mulgikapsas maitseb järgmisel päeval veelgi paremini, nii et tee seda julgelt varem ette ja soojenda aeglaselt üles.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: need ei küpse 20 minutiga läbi ja jäävad lõhe all toorelt krõmpsuvaks.
Ära pane kartuleid ahju ilma õli ja soolata: viilud kleepuvad ahjuplaadi külge ning jäävad kuivaks ja mõrult tuhmiks.
Ära jäta lõhe nahka ja kuiva pinda tähelepanuta: märg filee aurutab ennast ning muutub kartulitel hallikaks ja vesiseks, mitte õrnalt küpseks.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee paberrätikuga ja lase see enne ahju panekut 10 minutit toasooja käes seista, siis küpseb ta ühtlasemalt ja jääb mahlasemaks.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 3–4 mm: paksemad ei küpse 20 minutiga läbi ja jäävad lõhe all toorest.
Ära pane kartuleid ilma õli või võita ahjuplaadile: viilud kleepuvad külge ja ei pruunistu.
Ära pane lõhet külmkapi külmana otse kuumadele kartulitele: kala küpseb ebaühtlaselt ja äär kuivab, kui keskosa on veel toores.
output.tip: Kontrolli lõhe küpsust kahvliga paksemast kohast: kui liha laguneb kergelt helbeteks ja seest on 52–55 °C, on kala mahlane ja valmis.

pitfalls: Ära lõika kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: paksemad viilud ei küpse 20 minutiga läbi ja jäävad lõhe all toorest.
Ära pane kartuleid ahjuplaadile ilma õli või võita: viilud kleepuvad plaadi külge ja kuivavad servadest ära.
Ära pane lõhet kartulitele kohe sooja ahjust võetud kuumuses külmkapi külmana: jäine filee küpseb ebaühtlaselt ja välimine osa kuivab enne, kui keskosa valmis saab.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee paberkäterätiga ja lõika portsjoniteks enne kartulite peale panemist, siis küpseb kala ühtlasemalt ja jääb mahlasem.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulavõid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna osaliselt kinni keeta ja taignasse tekivad tükid.
Ära küpseta pannkooke liiga kõrgel kuumusel: välimine pool kõrbeb, sisemus jääb toorena ja pannkook rebeneb keeramisel.
Ära vala pannile liiga palju taignat korraga: pannkoogid tulevad paksud ja kummised, mitte õhukesed ja õrnad.
output.tip: Kui tainas seisma jäänud, sega see enne küpsetamist kiiresti läbi ja lisa vajadusel 1–2 spl piima, siis on see õhukeste pannkookide jaoks parajalt vedel.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulavõid taignasse liiga kuumana: see võib munad osaliselt kokku keeta ja taigen jääb tombuline.
Ära pane taignat pannile enne, kui pann on korralikult kuum: pannkook imab rasva, jääb kahvatuks ja rebeneb ümberpööramisel.
Ära kalla pannile liiga palju taignat korraga: pannkook jääb paks ja kummine, mitte õhuke ja pitsiline.
output.tip: Määri esimese pannkoogi jaoks pann õhukeselt võiga ja järgmistel pühi pinda vaid vähese võiga, siis saavad pannkoogid ühtlaselt kuldsed.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulavõid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna kerkima panna ja taigen hakkab tükkima, nii et sulata või ja lase enne lisamist veidi jahtuda.
Ära kalla taigent pannile liiga palju korraga: pannkook jääb paks ja kummine ning ei küpse keskelt läbi, 60–70 ml ühe pannkoogi kohta on paras.
Ära keera pannkooki liiga vara: kui serv pole veel kuldne ja pind kuiv, rebeneb see ümberpööramisel, nii et oota 1–2 minutit ja keera alles siis.
output.tip: Kui taignasse jäävad tombud, kurna see enne seismist läbi sõela, siis saad siledad pannkoogid ilma pikema vispeldamiseta.
